builds.title: The cinder block hot tub: can a fire under a stock tank make a spa?
builds.dek: A steel stock tank perched on a ring of cinder blocks with a fire roaring underneath makes a cozy reel; built that way it scorches, sags and overheats, but a tank with a side-mounted heater works.
builds.line: As filmed it is a cooking pot with people in it; on a full pad with a side heater and a thermometer, it is a fine soak.

builds.title: A shipping container buried in the backyard is a bunker waiting to cave in
builds.dek: Reels show a steel box dropped in a hole and covered over as a secret room, but a container's roof and walls were never meant to hold back soil, and the air inside runs out fast.
builds.line: A bare buried container is a crushing and suffocation hazard; the only safe version puts it inside an engineered concrete vault, and that is a contractor job.

builds.title: The soda-bottle garden tower: can a column of bottles feed you?
builds.dek: A stack of cut plastic bottles on a fence, bursting with lettuce and strawberries, is a feed favorite; as shown it would dry out by afternoon, but a post-mounted, drip-fed version is a proven extension design.
builds.line: As filmed the bottles hold about a day of water and cook in the sun; painted, post-mounted and drip-fed, the tower is a real, cheap garden.

builds.title: The bedroom with a window into the pool: could you dig one yourself?
builds.dek: Reels show a shovel, some concrete and a sheet of glass turning a backyard into an underwater lounge; done that way it is a room that can flood in seconds, and only an engineered, professional-led version is safe.
builds.line: As filmed it is a flood trap; engineered and professionally built it is real, but it is a six-figure project, not a weekend dig.

builds.title: The plastic bottle pool: could you build the viral reel?
builds.dek: A backyard pool walled with thousands of water bottles and a skin of cement racks up likes. Filled, it would let go all at once, but a round, footed version can work.
builds.line: As filmed it is a wall, not a pool; round, footed and lined, it becomes a real project.
